messages.author: fa6f5d4c13c0cca5
messages.subject: Model crashes when sampling
parts:
I'm having serious trouble running a model that should be pretty simple.

The model compiles (with Boost warnings that appear to be standard at this time); however, the process hangs when it begins sampling. I've tried this on two different computers; one completely locks the system (requiring a hard restart) and the other kills the process after a few seconds.  This happens every time I run the model.

Can anyone give me an idea about what's happening here?  I've tried a few variants of this model, all of which have the same result.  I haven't noticed this in the other models I've run. 

The model is essentially a two-way ANOVA with a binomial likelihood; coefficient for each factor (and their interaction) is modeled with a common variance term for shrinkage.

# Run Script
# setwd(...)
source("dat_list.RDump")
library(rstan)
sessionInfo()

fit = stan("crash_model.stan", data = dat_list, chains = 2, iter = 1500, cores = 1)

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model crashes when sampling
parts:
Have you tried running a small simulated data set on
a single chain? Stan shouldn't be crashing the system no
matter what happens. But if a single iteration takes
1000 leapfrog steps, it can get hung up in one iteration
and that's the granularity we current check for interrupts.
You can try setting the max tree depth lower to see if that
still crashes---if not, you may just be crushing the memory
of the system you're on.

- Bob

Thanks for the suggestion.

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model crashes when sampling
parts:
Model misspecification and/or bad initial values can cause lots
of problems in sampling. That's why we often find the hierarchical
priors make things go faster because they work out the right scale
for variables.

- Bob
